counterfactual_missing_items: Negative staining for: Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus
Hematoxylin-eosin staining demonstrated concentric proliferation of ovoid tumor cells present around small vessels over a hyalinized background stroma
decisive_items: concentric proliferation of ovoid tumor cells present around small vessels
CD31 immunostain highlighted many endothelial-lined vascular channels
Smooth muscle actin (SMA) was diffusely positive in the tumor cells
response.rationale: R3 is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of tumor cells around small vessels, positive CD31 immunostain, and positive smooth muscle actin staining, which are characteristic of angiosarcoma. R4 is less likely due to the contradictory histopathology findings and the lack of support for squamous cell carcinoma in the provided text.

rejected.why: Negative staining for Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus contradicts the diagnosis of Kaposi sarcoma.
